replies.text:
Step 2 checks:
- Automated abuse reachable: design has "the app calls POST /premium/unlock with the receipt" — an endpoint, but no sign-in, no email/SMS send, no data returned, no sign-up; mass unlocking is already covered by listed threats 1 and 4.
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing user-supplied content: design mentions no such screen — not applicable.
- Privileged actions without a record: "unlocks premium for the account" is granted with no transaction record — covered by listed threat 5.
- Cacheable personal/financial documents or pages: design describes no document or page response — not applicable.
- Attacker-controlled text into logs, CSV, emails, headers: design states no logging, export or email path for the receipt — not applicable.
- Single-reviewer threat (entitlement persists after refund/cancellation): real here — design grants premium on "a purchase succeeds" with no stated link to ongoing store state, a money harm distinct from the listed free-unlock and replay threats — not covered.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["mobile app", "POST /premium/unlock", "entitlement store"],
    "dataStores": ["account entitlement record"],
    "externalServices": ["app store"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["mobile client to server"],
    "dataClasses": [],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Premium stays unlocked after refund or cancellation, enabling buy-and-refund cycles",
      "scenario": "A customer buys premium so the app calls POST /premium/unlock, the server unlocks premium for the account, then the customer requests a store refund or lets the purchase lapse. The design describes a one-time unlock driven by the client's success call with no re-check against store state, so the entitlement stays on the account after the money is returned. Repeating buy-and-refund gives permanent premium at no cost, and many users can do it once the trick is shared.",
      "component": "POST /premium/unlock entitlement grant",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "medium", "reach": "many", "harm": "money" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "When a purchase succeeds the app calls POST /premium/unlock with the receipt." },
        { "quote": "The server trusts the client flag \"purchased\": true and unlocks premium for the account." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.4.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-840"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone can buy premium, get a refund, and keep premium forever because the server never re-checks whether the purchase is still valid.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Re-validate entitlement against current store state",
        "given": "an account whose premium was unlocked from a store purchase",
        "when": "the purchase is refunded, cancelled or expires, or the entitlement is next used",
        "then": "the server re-checks the purchase state with the store (including refund/cancellation notifications) and revokes premium when the purchase is no longer valid"
      }
    }
  ]
}
